Thermite-Microkernel exists: a verified microkernel by Thermite's author, pinned one commit before the bootable-kernel work Bulla forked. 2649 lines of Thermite, a five-level refinement chain, and a release rule blocking slag, proof holes, L0-L2, assume, axioms, external_body, unverified assembly and #[boundary]. Ahead of Bulla on proof content; Bulla is ahead on evidence mechanism. Not a rivalry: a microkernel's data model never nests types, so it never finds G4.

TMK's shape is step(state: flat struct, event: payload enum) -> (state, action) — a Mealy machine where composition lives in enum variants rather than struct fields, which is why G4 never fires there. Bulla converged on the same shape from the composition-cost argument rather than by adoption.

Locality and disjointness are the same discipline at two levels: the architecture says a subsystem's invariant must not mention another's state, and region-typed effects say a function must not touch another region. Regions are subsystems. So the decision that makes proofs cheap is the one that makes the concurrency check pass trivially — one choice buys both, and a kernel not built that way will have both rejected.

docs/architecture.md rewritten from Bulla's own analysis, then reconciled with docs/the-ladder.md. The meso line is drawn by invariant locality; #[boundary] is dropped from the core because boundaries make the trusted base grow at the same rate as the verified core; the claim closes at to_actions, a weaker coordinate than to_platform. Position restated as a rung rather than a fixed point.
